placement.position_note: Interpretive placement on a GENERATED lot, not a recovered parcel. The lot geometry is the K7 plat module's — this project has never read Thompson's numbering off a sheet, and the side lot lines and the alley are conjectural even where the block face is not. The building stands 7.5 m back from its street edge, which is a typology for the period and not a measurement of this lot. The whole footprint — not its centre — is tested against the platted street corridors, against its own lot lines and against every other footprint in the dataset, so no invented building of this parcel stands in the roadway; clearing the roadway is not the same as standing on a recovered lot.

siding_exposure_m.note: INVENTED WITHIN A STOCK SET, NOT DERIVED. No source states the exposed face of any Chicago building's siding. The value is one of four period mill sidings — 4.5, 5, 5.5 or 6 in to the weather; this roof wears 5.5 in — dealt in this building's own parcel recipe: drawn on this record's stable key from the stocks its household class may hang (5 in, 5.5 in or 6 in; T-1839, docs/LIBERTIES.md L352), then advanced within them so that no roof of the parcel standing within 60 m hangs the same course. It is NOT keyed to a construction season the way the named buildings' stocks are: this record's 1835-01-01 is the programme's count-unit convention and not a date anything was built, so keying to it would deal every anonymous roof in the town one stock. The separation is the surface variety T-0049 reconstructs, not a claim about 1835. docs/LIBERTIES.md L148 owns the invention and the recipe half is recorded beside it, under `tools/siding_stock.py`.

persons.name: Willinm Bandle
persons.note: PROJECTED RESIDENT. Documented in Chicago post-office evidence but not independently corroborated strongly enough for attested circa-1835 residence. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Bandle, Willinm' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 1 July 1835, column 4 — dated 1835-07-01. Nothing else in the corpus names this person: no trade, no street, no household, no arrival, so every other claim here is written unattested in its own block. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

residents.research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). persons.name: Amos Nichols
persons.note: RECONSTRUCTED, NOT FOUND, AND NOT CLAIMED AS KIN. This person is in the house and nothing says how. The population model places older children out of their parents' houses as apprentices and servants, and the head of this one is not old enough to be their parent, so the record says `household_member` and stops there rather than inventing a relation. A source naming this household retires them. No figure is drawn (L1).

residents.research_note: RECONSTRUCTED HOUSEHOLD — no trade recorded, in the south division. NOBODY HERE IS NAMED BY ANY SOURCE. The 1840 Chicago schedule counts children under ten at 27% of the town and women of twenty to twenty-nine as its second-largest band; the 1835 layer the sources can name holds 15 women, because the rolls that name this town — a letter list, a voters' roll, a subscription — print men. That gap is the shape of the evidence and not a reading of the town, so the order book counts it bucket by bucket and this household is drawn against those counts. Every value on it carries the model row and the seed that redraws it, and a source naming a woman who kept her own house in this division retires the whole record. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1).

citations.citation: Chicago · July 1835: Building Inventory and Architectural Reconstruction Specification. Prepared for Kevin Haas, August 2026.
what_it_supplies: A 665-roof production target with independently reconcilable group, district, level, and construction totals.
Thirty-five architectural family definitions with dimensional and massing bands.
District character, spacing, variation, finish, and chronology constraints for a July 1835 reconstruction.
A required distinction between named documentary landmarks and anonymous inferred infill.
what_it_does_not_supply: A surviving July 1835 building census or parcel-by-parcel roof register.
Exact locations, dimensions, appearance, occupants, or construction dates for anonymous roofs.
Authority to replace stronger building-specific evidence already represented in the dataset.

research_note: RECONSTRUCTED / GENERATED, NOT AN ATTESTED NAMED BUILDING. The block, its scheduled roof count and its family mix follow the 665-roof programme; exact presence, lot, position, footprint, finish and instance-level form are interpretive.

fabric_basis.words: new-sawn clapboard on a balloon frame, 9-over-6 sash of 6 × 8 in glass, plain corner boards and a stoop, under a new roof — a two-room frame cottage, new-built (rule F-T: a tradesman's by its type)
